title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in Part II of the 'Longue Marche' notes ('variations sur l'équation des lacets'), Grothendieck studies group schemes M_{ρ,σ}. The previous page writes M_{ρ,σ}(ℤ) as a semidirect product (ℤ/4×D_4)·Sl(2,ℤ). These groups are symmetry groups attached to the loop relations, built from tori T_ρ, T_0 and torus normalisers N'_σ.

The page begins by finishing a sentence: a homomorphism on integer points is 'pas surjectif' (not surjective).

It then computes the centre of M_{ρ,σ} = M_{ρ,σ}(0)·SG, a semidirect product with SG (an SL_2-type group) normal.

1. First claim. The centre is the direct product of two pieces:
 - the subgroup of the centre of M(0) that acts trivially on SG (and is fixed under M), and
 - the centre of SG, which is μ_2 and on which M acts trivially.

2. Applying the claim. He identifies M(0) ≅ Γ_{ρ,σ} ⊂ B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ.
 - He uses B'_0 ∩ μ_2 = {1} (μ_2 being the centre of SG), numbered (4.6).
 - He concludes that the part of Γ_{ρ,σ} acting trivially on SG is the subgroup (4.7): {(1, a, b) : (det a)^2 = 1, det b = 1}, with a ∈ T_ρ and b ∈ N'_σ.

3. Remaining task: find the centre of Γ_{ρ,σ}.
 - Γ_{ρ,σ} is an extension of μ_2×μ_2 by Γ°_{ρ,σ} ≅ G*_{ρ,σ}(0) ⊂ T°_0 × T_ρ × N_σ.
 - Γ° is commutative, so it suffices to compute the action of μ_2×μ_2 on Γ° and take invariants.
 - A bottom-margin note says this gives at least the intersection of the centre with Γ°.

4. Self-correction. A left-margin note flags that the general claim is false: non-trivial elements (g,f) of a semidirect product can be central without each component acting trivially on the other factor. A second note ('mais !' / 'vrai !') marks hesitation.

The next page carries out the invariant computation. μ_2×μ_2 acts through its first projection, by σ ↦ εσ on T_σ. The centre therefore lies in the kernel 𝒯'_{ρ,σ} of the map to μ_2.
errors: The opening claim, Z(H⋉N) = (Z(H)^{acting trivially, N-fixed}) × Z(N)^H, is false in general. Elements (h,n) with h acting on N as the inner automorphism inn(n^{-1}) and h central modulo the relevant condition can be central without either component being central or acting trivially. Grothendieck himself flags this in the left margin.

This is relevant here: on the previous page τ_∞ acts on Sl(2) by conjugation by diag(-1,1). That is inner for GL_2, though not by an element of SL_2(ℤ). So the counterexample mechanism must be checked case by case, and the identification of the centre is incomplete as written.

ideas.what: Computation of the centre of a semidirect product of a 'torus/normaliser' group with SL_2, via invariants of a finite μ_2×μ_2 action on a commutative group
ideas.modern_name: centre of semidirect products / group cohomology bookkeeping for algebraic group schemes

ideas.what: Group schemes M_{ρ,σ} as symmetry groups of the 'équation des lacets' (loop relations of the Teichmüller tower)
ideas.modern_name: automorphism group schemes related to Lego/Teichmüller tower relations, cf. GT relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); developed by Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps in other forms
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only alludes to the Teichmüller tower; these specific group schemes are not known in print

deep.surprise_reason: Routine computation of a centre inside a longer unpublished calculation, with a self-corrected group-theoretic slip. No new result or connection on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: Left-margin note is likely 'Faux ! des éléments ≠ 1 (g,f) d'un produit semi-direct peuvent être dans le centre, sans que les composantes opèrent trivialement…', i.e. a self-correction rather than 'Jamais…'.
The scratched first factor in '( ? × T_ρ × N'_σ)' is effectively 1 (B'_0 is replaced by its trivial part), consistent with (4.7).
'Γ°_{ρ,σ} ≅ G*_{ρ,σ}(0) ⊂ T°_0 × T_ρ × N_σ': the last factor is N_σ (possibly N'_σ or N°_σ), consistent with the next page.
